exam.title: Certified in Cybersecurity
exam.study_prerequisites: No work experience is required. Build connected risk/control reasoning across CIA, AAA, privacy, governance, BC/DR, identity lifecycle and access models, packet and cloud responsibility paths, data/asset protection, monitoring/triage, incident response and authorized testing against the September 1, 2026 outline.

review.notes: Every September 1, 2026 objective and weight is mapped through asset/business process, threat/vulnerability/risk, selected control, owner, evidence and response/recovery. New governance, IAM, network/cloud, testing/metrics and embedded AI-security boundaries are explicit. Three scenarios, eight authorized labs and 40 checks are included. Five URLs are reachable; two O'Reilly and two Udemy pages are automation-blocked; none are broken. No recalled/live item, dump or unauthorized test is used.

findings.title: The monitored change is editorial rather than a new blueprint
The actual outline confirms detailed scope and rounding
CAT length and course scores cannot predict the exam outcome
Suggested annual CPEs are not the required three-year total
AI context extends existing domains rather than adding a sixth
Password rules need scope and phishing-resistance distinctions
Network location and device ownership do not supply authorization
Successful sanitization operation still requires an adequacy decision
The latest NIST incident-response reference supersedes Revision 2
Post-quantum algorithm names describe different purposes

local_validation.execution_boundary: Actual SQLite backup/restore across four in-memory connections plus controlled IAM/alert/fictional timeline arithmetic. No files,credentials,network,OSaccounts,scans,media wiping orcloud.
local_validation.model_limits: Trusted identity/token and manifest fixtures,notJWT/authentication. No crashdurability/concurrency/encryption/malware-free/immutablebackup/forensiccustody/externaleffects guarantee. Exercise RTO/RPO times notactual runtime;five synthetic alerts notproductionquality.

limitations: Four commercial catalogs returned HTTP403; earlier durations,revision dates and complete alignment remain unverified. No book,video,paid lesson,practice question,checkout or enrollment was accessed.
Eight infrastructure labs and three scenarios remain proposed. Independent human review is pending; no real identity,network,cloud,incident-response or forensic exercise was executed.

34 checks run actual in-memory SQLite backup/restore and synthetic IAM/metric fixtures. No crash durability,concurrency,encrypted/immutable backup,malware-free recovery,complete chain of custody or external dependency proof.

Token/identity inputs and expected manifest are trusted fixtures. The workbook is not an authenticator or signature verifier; fictional RTO/RPO times are not actual measured copy time. Synthetic alert fractions are not detector accuracy.

Canonical web/PDF detailed objectives agree but introductory old domain names,testing-center wording and an impossible appointment date remain vendor presentation inconsistencies. Use actual booking availability.
Actual8-page outline fully read;AI29-pagePDF only introduction/CCsection. NIST references read selectively as recorded;not complete technical standards/compliance/legal audits.
No personal code/account entitlement,AMF/CPE eligibility,regionalprice,accommodation,coursequality or productionvendorbehavior was verified. Public policy is dated evidence,not an enrollment action.
Reserved five GitHub guides and disabled notification pilot remain untouched;no external messages,service/auth/logging changes or new permissions.

public_objective_groups.title: Domain 1: Security Principles
objectives:
1.1 - Understand cybersecurity concepts
Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Authentication, Authorization, Accounting (AAA)
Non-repudiation
Privacy

1.2 - Understand risk management concepts
Risk management lifecycle
Risk management processes

1.3 - Understand governance concepts
Regulations and laws
Frameworks and guidelines
Policies, standards (e.g., International Organization for Standardization (ISO), Center for Internet Security), procedures

1.4 - Understand cybersecurity controls
Technical controls
Administrative controls
Physical controls

1.5 - Maintain professional and ethical conduct
Professional code of conduct
Due care and due diligence
ISC2 Code of Ethics

public_objective_groups.title: Domain 2: Security Governance
objectives:
2.1 - Plan Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC)
Purpose
Importance
Frameworks and tools

2.2 - Understand redundancy
Business Continuity (BC)
Disaster Recovery (DR)

2.3 - Understand security awareness
Organizational culture (e.g., importance of security, security leadership)
Concepts (e.g., social engineering, password protection, phishing)

2.4 - Measure cybersecurity effectiveness
Key metrics, Key Risk Indicators (KRI)
Dashboards, score cards, reports

public_objective_groups.title: Domain 3: Identity And Access Management (IAM) Concepts
objectives:
3.1 - Understand identity life cycle management
Roles definition
Provision
Review
Deprovision
Frameworks and tools

3.2 - Understand logical access controls
Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)
Separation of Duties (SoD)
Access control models

public_objective_groups.title: Domain 4: Networking and Cloud Security Concepts
objectives:
4.1 - Understand network security
Concepts (e.g., Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) model, Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4), Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6), Virtual Private Network (VPN))
Firewalls (e.g., ports, applications)
Wireless (e.g., Wi-Fi, Bluetooth)
Embedded systems (e.g., Industrial Control System (ICS)), Internet Of Things (IoT)

4.2 - Understand network security architecture
Comprehending network segmentation (e.g., Firewall zones, Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN), micro-segmentation)
Defense in Depth
Zero Trust (ZT)

4.3 - Understand cloud security
Characteristics (e.g., Broad network access, rapid elasticity, measured service, on-demand self-service, resource pooling)
Service models
Deployment models
Shared security model (e.g., roles and responsibilities)

public_objective_groups.title: Domain 5: Security Operations and Incident Response
objectives:
5.1 - Understand data security
Data handling (e.g., classification, labeling, masking, and sanitization)
Encryption (e.g., symmetric, asymmetric, hashing, quantum resistant cryptography)

5.2 - Understand security operations
Logging and monitoring security events
Security event triage (e.g., incident use cases, prioritization, correlation)
Threat actors (e.g., types, motivations)
Cyber threat intelligence
Threat frameworks

5.3 - Understand Incident Response (IR)
Data handling policy implementing Incident Response Plan (IRP)
Incident Response (IR) exercises (e.g., testing, tabletop)

5.4 - Understand asset protection
Asset lifecycle management (e.g., End Of Life (EOL) software and devices)
Configuration and change management

5.5 - Understand security testing
Security readiness testing (e.g., blue teaming, purple teaming, red teaming)
Application testing (e.g., vulnerability scanning, static analysis, dynamic analysis, threat modeling)
Physical penetration testing (e.g., phishing, tailgating, impersonation)
